newsitem.title: ESTONIA: Key banks drag Estonian bourse to new highs.
newsitem.headline: Key banks drag Estonian bourse to new highs.

text.p: Estonian shares ended Wednesday at yet more fresh highs, boosted by rises in key banking stocks, despite starting slightly lower.
"It is as if people are afraid to let the market fall," one dealer said.
Total trade on the main list was a record-breaking 199.1 million kroons as the Talse index rose 2.15 kroons to a record 397.68 and started knocking on the door of the 400 level.
"Stocks fell amid technical problems in morning trade but leapt on the huge revision of the profit estimate by Hoiupank," one trader said.
Hoiupank hit 251 kroons after rising 14.25 kroons on trade worth 49.8 million kroons after it revised its 1997 profit forecast to 297.5 million kroons from 140 million kroons.
"The figure was more than we expected and perhaps Hoiupank is finding its true value now even at this high level," another trader said.
Hansapank also dipped in early trade to then follow Hoiupank's lead with a gain of 2.50 kroons to close at 225 kroons after turning over 56.8 million kroons.

Dealers said that reports that the St Petersburg tax police had ordered the freezing of several Estonian correspondent bank accounts affected some banks as it was seen as hitting their important Russian business, dealers said.
Forekspank, Tallinna Pank and EVEA Pank were the banks most affected, they added.
Forekspank said that it was appealing the decision in court, while Tallinna Pank said it was sending a delegation to the city to discuss the situation and seek further legal advice.
Forekspank was 3.25 kroons lower on the news at 229.50 and the release of the banks July profit at 8.1 did not left the stock's spirits.
"Foreks' result were very nice, but this St Petersburg news affected the price more," a dealer said. Tallinna Pank was also lower by 3.50 kroons to close on 66 kroons.
